subject: Latent growth change score model - unevenly spaced time points and adding exogenous predictors (time-varying and time-invariant)

messages.author: d80336c676cdbade
messages.subject: Latent growth change score model - unevenly spaced time points and adding exogenous predictors (time-varying and time-invariant)
parts:
Hi there, 

I am attempting to run a univariate latent growth change score model for a variable- IIPC- at 5 unevenly spaced time points (0, 3 months, 6 months, 12 months and 18 months). I would also like to include two time-invariant predictors (gender and age) and a time-varying predictor (SES - which is continuous). I also have another time-varying predictor which is dichotomous but I assume the script would be the same as the continuous time-varying predictor.

I believe I need to create two non-informative (or phantom) true scores with a single indicator fixed at 0 for the gap between 6 and 12 months and 12 and 18 months. However, I can't find any example script for including non-informative time points, nor can I find any examples of adding exogenous time-invariant or time-varying predictors in a latent growth change score model. I have had a go at altering the univariate change model lavaan script below based on MPLUS sytax extensions I have seen. 

Any help you anyone can provide confirming or correcting the syntax below would be greatly appreciated! Alternatively, if anyone does know of an article that provides lavaan script for these extensions please let me know!

Here is my go at extending the Lavaan script:

model.syntax <- "

# latent variables are indicated by the observed variables (also considered factor loadings)
ly1 =~ 1* IIPC.0 # ly1 is indicated by IIPC, factor loading = 1*
ly2 =~ 1* IIPC.1
ly3 =~ 1* IIPC.2
ly4 =~ 0* IIPC.0 ** Non-informative true score #1
ly5 =~ 1* IIPC.3
ly6 =~ 0* IIPC.0 ** Non-informative true score #2
ly6 =~ 1* IIPC.4


dy2 =~ 1 * ly2 # dy2 is indicated by ly2, factor loading = 1*
dy3 =~ 1 * ly3
dy4 =~ 1 * ly4
dy5 =~ 1 * ly5

# the constant change, g2, is indicated by dy2~dy6
g2 =~ 1*dy2 + 1*dy3 + 1*dy4 + 1*dy5

# factor means *
ly1 ~ 1
g2 ~ 1

# regressions
ly2 ~ 1 * ly1 + 1 * dy2 # ly2 is regressed on ly1 and dy2, regression coefficient is fixed at 1
ly3 ~ 1 * ly2 + 1 * dy3
ly4 ~ 1 * ly3 + 1 * dy4
ly5 ~ 1 * ly4 + 1 * dy5


# To examine the effect of a dichotmous (or continuous) exogenous predictor (time invariant covariate) on the intercept and slope
ly1 ~ GENDER_RS + Age_Constant_RS
g2 ~ GENDER_RS + Age_Constant_RS

 #variance of TIV covariates
GENDER_RS ~~ GENDER_RS
Age_Constant_RS~~ Age_Constant_RS

#covariance of TIV covaraites
Age_Constant_RS ~~  GENDER_RS

#means of TIV covariates (freely estimated)
Age_Constant_RS~ 1
GENDER_RS~ 1

# To examine the effect of a time-varying predictor (dichotomous and continuous)
dy2  ~ SES1
dy3 ~ SES2
dy4 ~ SES3
dy5 ~ SES4
dy6 ~ SES5
dy7 ~ SES6

#Constrain mean to 1
SES.2 ~ 1
SES.3 ~ 1
SES.4 ~ 1
SES.5 ~ 1
SES.6 ~ 1
SES.7 ~ 1
SES.8 ~ 1

#variance of TVC
SES2 ~~ theta2 * spring.2
SES3 ~~ theta2 * spring.3
SES4 ~~ theta2 * spring.4
SES5 ~~ theta2 * spring.5
SES6 ~~ theta2 * spring.6
SES7 ~~ theta2 * spring.7
SES8 ~~ theta2 * spring.8

# autoproportions, the changes of dy2 to dy7 is also proportional to ly1 to ly6, respectively
dy2 ~ pi * ly1 # dy2 is regressed on ly1, the regression coefficient is estimated as pi
dy3 ~ pi * ly2
dy4 ~ pi * ly3
dy5 ~ pi * ly4

# covariances among factors *
ly1 ~~ ly1
g2 ~~ g2
ly1 ~~ g2

ly2 ~~ 0*ly2  
ly3 ~~ 0*ly3  
ly4 ~~ 0*ly4  
ly5 ~~ 0*ly5    

dy2 ~~ 0*dy2
dy2 ~~ 0*dy3
dy2 ~~ 0*dy4
dy2 ~~ 0*dy5

dy3 ~~ 0*dy3
dy3 ~~ 0*dy4
dy3 ~~ 0*dy5

dy4 ~~ 0*dy4
dy4 ~~ 0*dy5

dy5 ~~ 0*dy5

# manifest variances (made equivalent by naming sigma2u)
IIPC.0 ~~ sigma2u*IIPC.0
IIPC.1 ~~ sigma2u*IIPC.1
IIPC.2 ~~ sigma2u*IIPC.2
IIPC.3 ~~ sigma2u*IIPC.3
IIPC.4 ~~ sigma2u*IIPC.4


# manifest means (fixed at zero)
IIPC.0 ~ 0
IIPC.1 ~ 0
IIPC.2 ~ 0
IIPC.3 ~ 0
IIPC.4 ~ 0
"
print(fitMeasures(fit, c("chisq", "df", "pvalue", "cfi", "rmsea"),
                  output = "text"), add.h0 = TRUE)

fit.lcs <- sem(model.syntax,
                data=functioningdata,
                missing         = "fiml",
                estimator       = "ml"
                )
summary(fit.lcs)

Thank you in advance for your help!!
